conventions.import: Import components from kit/index.ts and the styles once from kit/kit.css, after the brand token CSS.
conventions.className: Every component and part accepts className unless its entry says "className": false; className is never listed in props.
conventions.passthrough: Props not listed forward to the passthrough type, or to the props of the passthrough component; a listed one marked "x-from" (its library, ui-sdk or base-ui) is a passthrough prop worth knowing.
conventions.x-type: A prop JSON cannot carry: node (any React child), element (one React element), function, or object (a DOM node or a ref).
conventions.brands: Brands differ through token values only. There is no brand, theme or style variant prop.

Button.description: A button on UI SDK with a text label; while loading it ignores presses, stays focusable, is announced busy and keeps its width.

variant.description: primary: accent fill, one per view for the main action. secondary: layer fill with a hairline. quiet: text only.

size.description: m is 44px tall. s draws 32px and keeps a 44px hit area that reaches past its box.

loading.description: Shows a spinner over the label, blocks presses, stays focusable and sets aria-busy.

disabled.description: Blocks presses and removes the button from the tab order; prefer loading while an action is in progress.

focusableWhenDisabled.description: Keeps a disabled button in the tab order. The kit forces it on while loading, whatever you pass.

type.description: The native button type; set submit on the button that sends a form.

useWhen: A press runs an action on this page: save, send, delete, open a dialog.
Submitting a form, with type submit.

avoidWhen.text: The press goes to another page or URL.
The action has no words, only an icon.

a11y: Write a label that names the action (Save changes), not Click here or OK.
Give size s buttons at least var(--space-12) between neighbours, so each keeps its whole 44px hit area.
Keep the label while loading: it stays the accessible name.

IconButton.description: A square Button holding one icon and no visible text; it warns in development when it has no accessible name.

aria-label.description: The accessible name, naming the action: Undo, Close, Add orbit.

aria-labelledby.description: The id of a visible element that names the action, instead of aria-label.

useWhen: A familiar action in a toolbar or a dense row where the icon alone is understood: close, undo, more.

avoidWhen.text: The action needs words to be understood.
The press goes to another page or URL.

a11y: Give it an aria-label or aria-labelledby that names the action; the icon alone announces nothing.
Mark the icon svg aria-hidden="true" so it adds nothing to the name.
Give size s icon buttons at least var(--space-12) between neighbours, so each keeps its 44px hit area.

Card.description: A plain in-flow surface that groups related content on a raised layer; it has no role, no tab stop and no state of its own.

Root.description: The surface; it renders a div unless render swaps in another element such as section, article or li.

render.description: Replaces the div with another element, for example render={<article />} or render={<li />}.

Header.description: The top slot for a heading and an optional line under it; a heading placed here is sized as the card title.

Body.description: The main slot for text, fields or any content; long text wraps inside the card.

Footer.description: The bottom slot: a row of actions, aligned to the end, wrapping when it runs out of room.

useWhen: Content that belongs together and sits in the page flow: a summary, a settings group, a form step.
A repeated item in a list or grid, with render={<li />} inside a list.
Put actions in Card.Footer: a Button placed directly in the card stretches to the full card width.

avoidWhen.text: The content floats above the page and takes focus.
The whole surface is one link or button.

a11y: A card has no role; for one item or section, render it as article or section and name it with aria-labelledby.
Use a real heading in Card.Header at the level that fits the page outline.
Do not make the surface clickable; put a Button or a link inside it.

example.code:
// Golden example: the profile card of a crew member. An article named by its heading, a short // description, two fields to edit, and a row of actions. Spacing is token variables only. import { useId } from "react"; import { Button, Card, Field, Input } from "../index"; export default function CrewMemberCard() { const titleId = useId(); return ( } aria-labelledby={titleId}>

Ada Okafor

Flight engineer, Orbit 7

Joined the crew in March. Leads the docking checklist and the weekly systems review.

Role Call sign Shown on the crew roster. ); }

Checkbox.description: A checkbox on Base UI; inside Field.Root it takes the field's label, description, error and state, and shows a dash when mixed.

checked.description: Whether it is ticked, when you control it; pair with onCheckedChange. Use defaultChecked otherwise.

defaultChecked.description: Whether it starts ticked, when it manages its own state.

onCheckedChange.description: Called with the new checked value when the person ticks or unticks it.

indeterminate.description: Shows a dash and announces mixed, for a box that sums up a group that is partly ticked. It wins over checked.

disabled.description: Blocks toggling and removes it from the tab order. Field.Root disabled does the same and mutes the label.

required.description: Inside a Base UI Form, a submit without the tick is blocked and shows Field.Error match="valueMissing". Sets aria-required.

name.description: The name submitted with the form. Inside Field.Root, the field's name wins.

useWhen: One yes or no choice that takes effect when the form is sent: include charts, email me.
A tick the person must give before an action, such as agreeing to terms.

avoidWhen.text: Exactly one option of a set may be picked.
The choice runs an action the moment it is pressed.

a11y: Wrap the Checkbox and its text in Field.Label inside Field.Root, so the text names it and a click on it toggles.
For a required tick, set required and name, inside a Base UI Form, with Field.Error match="valueMissing".
Use indeterminate only on a box that sums up a group of boxes, and keep it in step with them.

Dialog.description: A modal dialog on Base UI: focus is trapped while open, Escape and an outside press close it, and focus returns to the trigger.

Root.description: Holds the open state; it renders no element of its own.

open.description: Controls the open state; pair it with onOpenChange.

defaultOpen.description: Opens the dialog on first render when the state is not controlled.

onOpenChange.description: Called with the next open state whenever the dialog asks to open or close.

Trigger.description: The button that opens the dialog; it renders a kit Button.

variant.description: The Button variant; unset, it is the Button default, secondary.

size.description: The Button size; unset, it is the Button default, m.

Popup.description: The backdrop, viewport and dialog box in one part, in a portal on document.body (a nested dialog's goes in its parent's).

container.description: The element, or a ref to it, the portal mounts into instead of document.body.

finalFocus.description: What takes focus on close: a ref, a function returning an element, or false. Needed when the trigger may be gone by then.

initialFocus.description: What takes focus on open: a ref, a function returning an element, or false. Default: the first tabbable element.

Header.description: A layout row for the title and the corner close control.

Title.description: The heading that names the dialog; Base UI points the popup's aria-labelledby at it.

Description.description: The supporting text; Base UI points the popup's aria-describedby at it.

Actions.description: A layout row for the dialog's buttons, at the end of the popup.

Close.description: A button that closes the dialog; it renders a kit Button unless render gives another element.

variant.description: The Button variant; unset, it is the Button default, secondary.

size.description: The Button size; unset, it is the Button default, m.

render.description: Another element to close with, in place of the kit Button.

CloseIcon.description: The corner close control, a quiet size s IconButton already named for screen readers.

label.description: The accessible name; change it only to translate it or to name what closes.

useWhen: A decision or a short task that must be finished or dismissed before going on: confirm a delete, rename.

avoidWhen.text: The content is long or is a page of its own.
A short message that needs no answer.

a11y: Give every Dialog.Popup a Dialog.Title; it is the dialog's accessible name.
If the trigger can unmount while the dialog is open, pass finalFocus on Dialog.Popup.
Offer a visible way out: a Dialog.CloseIcon in the header or a Dialog.Close in the actions.

Field.description: A labelled form field on Base UI that wires its label, description and error to the control inside it.

Root.description: Groups one control with its label, description and error, and holds the field's invalid and disabled state.

invalid.description: Marks the control aria-invalid and data-invalid (the heavy outline). It does not show Field.Error; that needs match.

disabled.description: Disables the control and mutes the label.

name.description: The control's name when the form is submitted.

Label.description: The visible label; it is the control's accessible name through a for/id pair set by Base UI.

Description.description: A hint below the control, joined to its aria-describedby.

Error.description: The error message, joined to aria-describedby; it renders only on match, a failed native check or a form error.

match.description: true renders it, even when disabled; a ValidityState key renders it while that native check fails. Use match={!!error}.

useWhen: Any text input, so it has a visible label, an optional hint and an error said in words.

avoidWhen.text: One question answered with several controls, such as a set of radios.

a11y: Give every Field.Root a Field.Label; a placeholder is not a label.
When the value is wrong, set invalid on Field.Root and match on Field.Error, and say what to fix in words.
Put format rules in Field.Description before the person types, not only in the error.

Input.description: A text input; inside Field.Root it takes the field's label, description, error and invalid and disabled state.

type.description: The native input type: text, email, password, search, tel, url, number.

readOnly.description: Shows a value that cannot be edited on a layer fill; it stays focusable and is still submitted.

autoComplete.description: The autofill hint, such as email, name or current-password.

useWhen: One line of text inside Field.Root: a name, an email, a URL, a search term.

avoidWhen.text: The text runs to more than one line.
The person picks from a fixed short list.

a11y: Place it inside Field.Root with a Field.Label; on its own it has no name unless you give it aria-label.
Set autoComplete on fields that ask for the person's own data, such as email or name.

Select.description: A select on Base UI: arrow keys and typing move the highlight, Enter picks, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger.

Root.description: Holds the value and the open state; it renders no element of its own.

items.description: Maps each value to its label, so the trigger shows the label and not the raw value.

value.description: The selected value when controlled; pair it with onValueChange. null shows the placeholder.

defaultValue.description: The value selected on first render when the value is not controlled.

onValueChange.description: Called with the next value whenever an item is picked.

disabled.description: Stops the select from opening or changing; inside Field.Root, Field.Root's disabled does the same.

name.description: The value's name when the form is submitted, if Field.Root does not give one.

required.description: A value must be chosen; inside Base UI's Form, submitting empty fails with valueMissing for Field.Error.

open.description: Controls the open state; pair it with onOpenChange.

modal.description: Unset, true: while open, page scroll locks and outside presses only close. false leaves the page usable.

Trigger.description: The button that opens the list; it shows the selected label or the placeholder, with the Input's look.

placeholder.description: Shown, muted, while nothing is selected. It is not a label; Field.Label still names the select.

Popup.description: Portal, positioner, popup and list in one part; it opens below the trigger, at least as wide, on document.body.

container.description: The element, or a ref to it, the portal mounts into instead of document.body.

side.description: The trigger's side the popup opens on; unset, Base UI's bottom. It flips when there is no room.

align.description: The popup's alignment along that side; unset, Base UI's center.

sideOffset.description: Extra px on top of the kit's CSS offset. Neither applies when alignItemWithTrigger lays the popup over the trigger.

collisionPadding.description: Kit-set: the 8px gap the popup keeps from the window's edges, the Dialog's gutter. Base UI's is 5.

alignItemWithTrigger.description: Kit-set off: the popup opens below the trigger. On, it covers the trigger with the selected item over the value.

finalFocus.description: What takes focus on close: a ref, a function returning an element, or false. Default: the trigger.

Item.description: One option; its text is the label used for typeahead, and a check in the text colour marks the selected one.

value.description: The value this item stands for; one of the keys of Root's items.

disabled.description: Shows the item muted and stops it from being picked.

label.description: The text typeahead matches, when it should differ from the item's visible text.

Group.description: Groups related items under a GroupLabel.

GroupLabel.description: The muted heading of a group; Base UI points the group's aria-labelledby at it.

useWhen: One choice from a fixed list of about five to twenty-five options, inside a form.
The options are known up front and need no search.

avoidWhen.text: Two to four options that fit on screen at once.
The person may type a value that is not in the list.
The list starts an action instead of choosing a value.

a11y: Put it inside Field.Root with a Field.Label; the placeholder is not a label.
Pass items on Root so the trigger reads the label, not the raw value.
When nothing valid is chosen, set invalid on Field.Root and say what to fix in Field.Error.

Switch.description: A switch on Base UI whose thumb slides to on; inside Field.Root it takes the field's label, description, error and state.

checked.description: Whether it is on, when you control it; pair with onCheckedChange. Use defaultChecked otherwise.

defaultChecked.description: Whether it starts on, when it manages its own state.

onCheckedChange.description: Called with the new value when the person turns it on or off.

disabled.description: Blocks toggling and removes it from the tab order. Field.Root disabled does the same and mutes the label.

name.description: The name submitted with the form, with the value "on" when on and nothing when off. Inside Field.Root, the field's name wins.

uncheckedValue.description: The value submitted when it is off. Without it, an off switch submits nothing, as a native checkbox does.

useWhen: A setting that is on or off and stays that way, such as notifications or grid lines.
A row in a settings list, where the label says what turns on.

avoidWhen.text: The person must tick before an action, such as agreeing to terms.
Exactly one option of a set may be picked.
The press runs an action once, not a setting that stays.

a11y: Wrap the Switch and its text in Field.Label inside Field.Root, so the text names it and a click on it toggles.
Name what turns on (Show grid lines), never the state: the switch already says on or off.

Tabs.description: Tabs on UI SDK: a row of tabs that each show one panel, moved through with the arrow keys, Home and End.

Root.description: Holds the selected value and groups the list and the panels, in one horizontal row.

value.description: The selected tab's value, when you control it; pair with onValueChange. Use defaultValue otherwise.

defaultValue.description: The tab selected first, when it manages its own state. Unset, the first enabled tab.

onValueChange.description: Called with the newly selected tab's value.

List.description: The row of tabs, with the selected bar drawn under the selected tab.

activateOnFocus.description: Select a tab as the arrow keys reach it. Off by default: arrows move focus, Enter or Space selects.

Tab.description: One tab: a button that shows its panel when selected.

value.description: Names the tab; the Panel with the same value is the one it shows.

disabled.description: Blocks selecting the tab. The arrow keys still reach it, so a screen reader announces it as unavailable.

Panel.description: The content one tab shows, in the page only while its tab is selected unless keepMounted is set.

value.description: The value of the Tab that shows this panel.

keepMounted.description: Keep the panel in the page, hidden, while another tab is selected, so its state survives.

useWhen: Two to six views of one thing, where the person reads one at a time: overview, moons, history.
Sections that sit side by side on one page and do not need their own address.

avoidWhen.text: Each view is a page of its own that people link to or go back to.
The choice changes a setting or filters data rather than showing a section.
The person needs to compare the sections at once.

a11y: Name every Tabs.List with aria-label, or aria-labelledby on a visible heading.
Give each Tab a Panel with the same value; the panel takes the tab's name.
Keep tab labels short and plain text: no icons without a label, no buttons inside a tab.

Textarea.description: Multi-line text; inside Field.Root it takes the field's label, description, error and invalid and disabled state.

rows.description: Visible lines before the text scrolls. The person can still drag the box taller.

readOnly.description: Shows a value that cannot be edited on a layer fill; it stays focusable and is still submitted.

placeholder.description: A hint shown while empty. It does not replace the label.

onValueChange.description: Called with the new text on each edit. Use it to control the value.

useWhen: Free text that runs to several lines: a note, a message, a description, feedback.

avoidWhen.text: The text is one line: a name, an email, a URL.

a11y: Place it inside Field.Root with a Field.Label; on its own it has no name unless you give it aria-label.
Say any length or format limit in Field.Description before the person types, not only in the error.
